title.narrative: Sustainable Landscape through Integrated Management (SLIM)

description.narrative:
The action contributes to enhance resilience of ecosystems and improve people¿s livelihoods based on integrated landscape approaches along the agriculture-forestry-biodiversity-water and climate nexus.

The Action aims to assist Zambia in putting its 8th National Development Plan (8NDP) and Vision 2030 into action. It will focus on two main areas of the landscape: a) the Greater Kafue area, and b) the Lower Zambezi-South Luangwa-North Luangwa-part of the Nyika Plateau area.

The main goal is to contribute to increase resilience of landscape/ecosystems and improve people¿s livelihoods based on the integrated land approach along agriculture-forestry-biodiversity-water and climate nexus. The action¿s specific objectives are:

1.Strengthening governance mechanisms, policies, and coordination for integrated landscape management and climate adaptation, and

2.Enhancing technical and technological capacities for integrated landscape management and climate adaptation.

To achieve these objectives, the Action will focus on 4 main intervention areas: Under Output 1.1. it will support policy and regulatory framework development to reinforce ILM policy delivery by supporting revision and/or development of policies/strategies and regulations needed for integrated and sustainable management of ecosystems. Output 1.2 targets enhancement of collaboration, coordination, and participation mechanisms among stakeholders for decision-making in ILM as well as contributing to the EU-Zambia Forest Partnership implementation. Ministry of Finance and National Planning, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Ministry of Green Economy and Environment, Ministry of Technology and Science, SMART Zambia Institute and Ministry of Tourism feature among the expected project partners and beneficiaries.

The Action will strengthen technical and institutional tools for ILM implementation (Output 2.1.) through promoting jointly developed data products, maps and tools. Specific focus is placed on geospatial data utilization and development of sustainable forest management plans. Finally, under the Output 2.2. the action will contribute to improvement of institutional capacity for planning, management and monitoring of integrated landscape through technical assistance to line Ministries as well as their specialized departments such as the Forestry Department and the National Remote Sensing Centre.
